note: Recorded example results from the fictional Larkspur Labs demo (demo/). Shown when the live demo database is unavailable. Snippets are copied from demo/data.

results.title: ADR-0012: Replace Elasticsearch with Postgres full-text search
results.snippet: Proposal to supersede ADR-0005. Background: the 2025-12-04 reindex incident (postmortem in larkspur/api), the evaluation in larkspur/api#32 and the benchmark spike in larkspur/api#38. TL;DR: 2.1M reports (not 10M), p95 38 ms on Postgres FTS vs 22 ms on ES,…

results.title: INCIDENT: search missing a large share of reports
results.snippet: Brightwell reports that searches return far fewer results than yesterday. ES doc count is 1.56M vs 1.90M reports in Postgres (~18% missing). Last night's full reindex looks stuck. Investigating.

results.title: Postmortem: 2025-12-04 search reindex outage
results.snippet: Blameless postmortem for #29. Action item 3 is the big one: evaluate whether we need Elasticsearch.

results.title: Elastic Cloud bill went from $640 to $1,380/month
results.snippet: After scaling to 3 nodes during the 2025-12-04 incident, the Elastic Cloud deployment costs $1,380/month. Scaling back to 2 nodes saves ~$740 but brings back the disk watermark problem during reindexes. Keep 3 nodes?

results.title: Evaluate replacing Elasticsearch with Postgres full-text search
results.snippet: Postmortem action item 3. Questions to answer: 1. Latency: can Postgres FTS meet our 150 ms p95 budget on production-sized data? 2. Relevance: do top-10 results match ES closely enough on real queries? 3. Fuzzy address matching: how much do we lose? 4. Cost…

examples.query: Why did we move off Auth0?

results.title: ADR-0013: WorkOS for auth, SSO and SCIM (supersedes ADR-0004)
results.snippet: Enterprise deals are blocked on SAML SSO and SCIM (larkspur/api#45). Auth0's Enterprise quote plus SCIM add-on doesn't fit our pricing; WorkOS charges per SSO connection, which we can pass through in the enterprise plan. Migration: import Auth0 password…

results.title: WorkOS: AuthKit sign-in, SSO and Directory Sync (SCIM)
results.snippet: Implements ADR-0013 on the API side. /v1/auth/callback exchanges the WorkOS code for a session; API verifies WorkOS JWTs SSO: organizations map to our firms; domain verification required Directory Sync webhooks create/deactivate inspectors (and update Stripe…

results.title: Migrate Auth0 users to WorkOS (import password hashes)
results.snippet: One-off migration: export Auth0 users with bcrypt hashes (Auth0 support ticket), import into WorkOS, map ids in users.workos_id. Users keep their passwords; Google logins re-link by verified email. Dry run on staging: 4,212 users, 0 failures.

results.title: ADR-0004: Auth0 for authentication
results.snippet: We shouldn't build password storage, resets and MFA ourselves. Auth0 Essentials covers email/password, Google login and MFA. The API verifies RS256 JWTs against the JWKS. Looked at Cognito (cheaper, but the hosted UI is rough and customizing it is painful)…

results.title: ADR-0010: Move from Heroku to AWS (ECS Fargate + RDS)
results.snippet: ADR-0003 said we'd revisit Heroku when the bill passed ~$2k/month or a customer needed private networking. Both happened: October bill: $2,912 (Performance-M dynos for PDF workers after the R14 errors) Brightwell Surveys (enterprise pilot) needs VPC peering →…

results.title: Heroku Postgres connection limit (120) reached at peak
results.snippet: Monday morning peak: FATAL: too many connections. Standard-0 caps at 120; web + workers + beat use ~110 at peak.

results.title: Heroku R14/R15 memory errors in the PDF worker
results.snippet: Since big firms started uploading 300+ photos per report, the pdf worker dynos hit R14 (memory quota exceeded) daily and R15 (killed) a few times a week. wkhtmltopdf loads every image at full resolution.

results.title: Plan: migrate from Heroku to AWS
results.snippet: ADR-0003's exit criteria are met (bill > $2k/month, enterprise customer needs private networking). Proposed plan: 1. Terraform: VPC, ECS Fargate (api, worker-default, worker-pdf), RDS Postgres 16 (multi-AZ), ElastiCache Redis, ALB, S3. 2. Logical replication…

examples.query: How do we rate limit the API?

results.title: Rate limit the public API with a Redis token bucket
results.snippet: Partners now call /v1 with API keys, and one partner's sync job sent 40k requests in 10 minutes last week. This adds a per-API-key token bucket in Redis (100 req/min burst, 20 req/s sustained), returns 429 with Retry-After, and exempts the PWA's session…

results.title: Proposal: move background jobs from Celery/Redis to a Postgres-backed queue?
results.snippet: Now that search lives in Postgres, Redis is only a Celery broker plus rate limiting. Options: keep Celery + Redis, or move jobs to a Postgres queue (procrastinate, or plain SKIP LOCKED) for transactional enqueueing. Not urgent, opening for discussion.

results.title: Add Celery worker with Redis broker
results.snippet: We need background jobs for ES indexing, emails and soon PDF rendering. This adds a Celery app with Redis as broker and result backend, a worker Procfile entry and beat for periodic jobs (the ES catch-up job). Why Celery over RQ or Dramatiq: we need retries…
